title: The blueprint's coefficient class supplies the restricted datum, with $c=2\dim\overline X$
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a chosen uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$ and the finite discrete ring $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, let $Y$ and $\overline X$ be finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with $\dim\overline X\leq d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $p:\overline X\to Y$ be a proper finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Then the class-restricted datum of [def-sf-fullcd-class] holds:
$$\operatorname{FullCD}_{\mathrm{cls}}(p,A;2d).$$
The coefficient class is the entire essential image of the comparison inverse image on étale $A$-module sheaves [def-sf-fullcd-used-class, def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with no constructibility condition. The same bound holds uniformly for the pullback of each original-source coefficient sheaf along every object $V\to Y$ of $Y_{\Proet}$, exactly as in clause 2 of [def-sf-fullcd-class]; no finite-type or dimension hypothesis is imposed on $V$.

If $\overline X$ is nonempty, one may take the intrinsic bound $2\dim\overline X\leq2d$. If $\overline X$ is empty (so $\dim\overline X=-\infty$), the nonnegative bound is $0$. The comparison direction has bound $M=0$ by [prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero]. For nonempty source the residual $2\dim\overline X$ is the étale direction of the Leray spectral sequence of [thm-sp-grothendieck], rather than a lower bound on $R^q\nu_{\overline X,*}$.

proof.text: The sheaf quantifier is identical in the two nodes. Indeed [def-sf-fullcd-used-class] says that membership is existence of an étale $A$-module sheaf $G$ and an isomorphism $\nu_{\overline X}^*G\cong\mathcal F$. The defining paragraph of [def-sf-fullcd-class] uses precisely the same witness and imposes no constructibility condition. Thus the two definitions specify exactly the same class of sheaves. No choice of witness changes the class.

source.place: Proof, sentences identifying the two coefficient-class quantifiers

proof.text: Fix such a sheaf $\mathcal F$ and $r>2d$. Apply the displayed vanishing of [thm-sf-fullcd-used-class] to the site object $V=Y$ with its identity morphism. The fibre product $\overline X\times_Y Y$ identifies with $\overline X$, its first projection is the identity, and its other projection is $p$. Consequently that vanishing is $\mathcal H_Y^r(Rp_*(\mathcal F[0]))=0$, the first clause of [def-sf-fullcd-class]. All the theorem's field, coefficient, finite-type, properness and original-source dimension hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses here.

source.place: Proof, sentence asserting the absolute clause

proof.text: Now let $v:V\to Y$ be any object of $Y_{\Proet}$. The displayed statement of [thm-sf-fullcd-used-class] applies to this $V$ and the same original-source sheaf $\mathcal F$, and gives $\mathcal H_V^r(R(p_V)_*((g_V^*\mathcal F)[0]))=0$ for every $r>2d$. This is exactly clause 2 of [def-sf-fullcd-class]. Its quantifier is not over arbitrary sheaves on $\overline X_V$. Thus no finite-type assertion about $V$ and no comparison of its dimension with $d$ is needed. Both defining clauses now hold with the same ring and bound, proving $\operatorname{FullCD}_{\mathrm{cls}}(p,A;2d)$.

source.place: Proof, sentences asserting the relative clause and identifying its quantifier

proof.text: For nonempty $\overline X$, the dimension convention [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and the assumed inequality with the nonnegative integer $d$ imply $m=\dim\overline X\in\{0,1,\ldots,d\}$. Apply [thm-sf-fullcd-used-class] with dimension parameter $m$: for every original-source sheaf $\mathcal F$ in the class, every site object $V\to Y$ and every $r>2m$, it gives $\mathcal H_V^r(R(p_V)_*((g_V^*\mathcal F)[0]))=0$. At $V=Y$ with its identity this is the absolute clause; at arbitrary $V$ it is the relative clause. These are the two clauses of [def-sf-fullcd-class] with parameter $2m$. If $r>2d$, then $r>2m$, so the same vanishings also give bound $2d$. For empty $\overline X$ the dimension is $-\infty\leq0$ by that definition, so the same theorem applies with $d=0$ and gives $\operatorname{FullCD}_{\mathrm{cls}}(p,A;0)$; one does not insert $-\infty$ as the parameter of [def-sf-fullcd-class].

source.place: Statement, intrinsic dimension bound, with the empty-source convention made explicit

proof.text:
Choose an origin witness $
u_{\overline X}^*G\cong\mathcal F$ using [def-sf-fullcd-used-class]. The ring $A$ is finite and discrete by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Apply [prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero] with $X=\overline X$: it gives $G\cong
u_{\overline X,*}\mathcal F$ and $R^b
u_{\overline X,*}\mathcal F=0$ for every $b>0$. This statement applies to arbitrary $G$, without assuming constructibility, and to arbitrary schemes. Hence the comparison bound is $M=0$ and has no dimension contribution.

proof.text:
Check the hypotheses for the spectral sequence with first functor $F=
u_{\overline X,*}$ and second functor $G_0=p_{\Et,*}$. The fixed-$A$ module categories on the three small sites are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], working in the larger universe in which the sites are small, and have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. The comparison adjunction is [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]; its left adjoint is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level]. The sectionwise restriction formula in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] carries addition and each scalar endomorphism to the same operations on sections, so its right adjoint is additive on fixed-$A$ modules. As a right adjoint it preserves kernels and finite products by their universal properties, hence is left exact. For an injective $I$ on $\overline X_{\Proet}$ and a monomorphism $M\hookrightarrow N$ on $\overline X_{\Et}$, exactness makes $
u^*M\hookrightarrow
u^*N$ monic. A map $M	o
u_*I$ corresponds to a map $
u^*M	o I$; extend it to $
u^*N$ by injectivity and transpose it back to $N	o
u_*I$. By [def-sp-injective-resolutions] this proves $
u_*I$ is injective. Use specifically the Module sheaves clause of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] with $R=A$: its constant-ring module direct image $p_{\Et,*}$ is additive and left exact and commutes with forgetting to abelian sheaves, and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing] then gives $R^a p_{\Et,*}(
u_*I)=0$ for $a>0$. Thus the required injective-to-acyclic condition holds.

source.place: Tag 015N, lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence: verification of the injective-to-acyclic hypothesis

proof.text: Apply [thm-sp-grothendieck] to the pair verified in Step 6. Its page is $E_2^{a,b}=R^a p_{\Et,*}(R^b\nu_{\overline X,*}\mathcal F)$ and it converges to $R^{a+b}(p_{\Et,*}\circ\nu_{\overline X,*})(\mathcal F)$. The first-quadrant double-complex convergence statement [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences], for the construction specified in [thm-sp-grothendieck], supplies a finite filtration in total degree $n$ with $F^0=H^n$, $F^{n+1}=0$ and graded pieces $E_\infty^{a,n-a}$. By [prop-sf-comparison-bound-zero], all rows $b>0$ are zero and the row $b=0$ is $R^a p_{\Et,*}G$. The cohomological differential has bidegree $(r,1-r)$. Induct on $r\geq2$: all positive rows vanish on page $2$, and a zero entry has zero kernel modulo image on the next page, so these rows remain zero. A differential out of $(a,0)$ has target $(a+r,1-r)$, outside the first quadrant; an incoming differential has source $(a-r,r-1)$, which is zero (or outside the quadrant). Thus the bottom row survives unchanged. In total degree $t\geq0$, all graded pieces of the finite filtration vanish except the piece with index $a=t$, which is $R^t p_{\Et,*}G$. Indeed $F^0=\cdots=F^t=H^t$ and $F^{t+1}=0$, so the abutment in degree $t$ is isomorphic to $R^t p_{\Et,*}G$. In this Leray calculation every remaining positive degree is therefore in the étale direct-image direction $a$, while the comparison direction $b$ is already bounded by $0$. This explains the residual dimension allowance of Steps 2–4 and excludes interpreting it as a positive lower bound on the comparison direct images. The argument does not claim $R^{2\dim\overline X}p_*$ must be nonzero, nor apply the dimension theorem afresh to a possibly non-finite-type base change.

source.place: Tag 015N, lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence, specialized to the comparison and étale direct image; Tag 099V eliminates all positive comparison rows

proof.text:
To relate this étale row to the pro-étale direct image in the conclusion, first check that $p$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Finite type gives quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Properness makes the diagonal a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]; over each affine $\operatorname{Spec}R$ in the target of the diagonal, its inverse image is the single affine $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ for an ideal $I$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The algebra $R/I$ is generated over $R$ by the empty set, and this single affine is a finite affine cover of the inverse image. The finite-affine-cover criterion in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] therefore makes the diagonal finite type, hence quasi-compact. This is quasi-separatedness [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. The bounded-below comparison below computes the total direct image used in the FullCD clauses: by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], a bounded-below injective resolution of $\mathcal F[0]$ is K-injective, so the same resolution computes both the bounded-below direct image and the unbounded finite-level functor defined in [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] to $p$ and $G[0]$ to get $Rp_{\Proet,*}\mathcal F\cong
u_Y^*Rp_{\Et,*}G$. Since $
u_Y^*$ is exact [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level], its application commutes with the kernels, images and quotients defining cohomology; thus $\mathcal H^a(Rp_{\Proet,*}\mathcal F)\cong
u_Y^*R^ap_{\Et,*}G$. It also detects vanishing: if $
u_Y^*M=0$, the unit isomorphism of the same node identifies $M$ with $
u_{Y,*}0=0$. The pro-étale vanishings of Steps 2–4 are therefore exactly vanishings in the surviving étale row of Step 7. This proves the asserted interpretation of the residual bound without attributing a positive degree to the comparison direction.
